paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: The variation curve of k^⊤β for AlphaEdit and MEMIT as the number of edits increases, with GPT2-XL serving as the edited model. As the results of Llama3-8B are not suitable for display in a line chart, they are presented in Appendix <ref>.
model_annotation: The plot titled “GPT2-XL” illustrates how the quantity \(k^\top \beta\) varies with the number of edits for two methods, AlphaEdit and MEMIT. The x-axis represents the number of edits on a linear scale, spanning from about 200 to 3000, with numeric tick labels shown at regular 500-step intervals (500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500, 3000). The y-axis is labeled \(k^\top \beta\) on a linear scale, ranging from 0 up to slightly above 0.012, with labeled ticks at approximately 0.002 intervals (0.002, 0.004, 0.006, 0.008, 0.010, 0.012). The AlphaEdit series is drawn as a solid red line with circular markers and decreases across the x-range, starting near 0.004 at ~200 edits and reaching about 0.0011 by 3000 edits, passing through intermediate points around 0.0025 (500), 0.0019 (1000), 0.0015 (1500), 0.0013 (2000), and 0.0012 (2500). The MEMIT series is drawn as a solid light-blue line with circular markers and increases across the x-range, starting near 0.0046 at ~200 edits and rising to about 0.0128 by 3000 edits, with intermediate values around 0.0052 (500), 0.0067 (1000), 0.0081 (1500), 0.0094 (2000), and 0.0106 (2500).
